meta.tagline: sourdough baked overnight, collected before nine
meta.description: A two-oven neighbourhood bakery. Naturally leavened sourdough, pre-ordered by Thursday and collected Saturday morning.

hero.headline: We bake 140 loaves. Then we stop.
hero.sub: Naturally leavened, 30-hour ferment, baked overnight Friday. Order by Thursday evening and collect between seven and nine on Saturday morning, still warm.
hero.note: Orders close Thursday at 8pm, or when the 140th loaf goes.
trust: Three ingredients in the country loaf

sections.heading: Four loaves, every week
sections.intro: The list does not change often. When it does, it is because something is in season, not because we are bored.

items.title: Country loaf
items.body: Flour, water, salt. A 30-hour ferment, baked dark. This is the one to buy first.

items.title: Seeded rye
items.body: Forty percent rye with toasted sunflower, flax and caraway. Dense, sour, keeps for most of a week.

items.title: Olive and rosemary
items.body: Kalamata olives and rosemary cut into the country dough. Good enough to eat standing over the sink.

items.title: Saturday cinnamon buns
items.body: Six to a tray, iced while warm. They go first, every single week, so order them with the bread.

items.title: Order by Thursday 8pm
items.body: Through the order link. Pay then, so the count is real and nothing is wasted.

items.title: We bake overnight Friday
items.body: Shaped Friday evening, in the oven at three, out by six.

items.title: Collect 7 to 9 Saturday
items.body: Your name is on the shelf. After nine, anything uncollected goes to whoever is in the queue.

sections.heading: Prices, and what a week costs

tiers.name: Single loaf
tiers.desc: Country, rye or olive. Pick at checkout.

tiers.name: Weekly standing order
tiers.desc: One loaf a week, your choice each week, never sold out.
includes: Held back before general orders open
tiers.fine: Cheaper than four singles, because we know the count in advance.

sections.heading: Asked at the door most weeks

items.a: You can, and some weeks there is bread left at half past eight. Most weeks there is not. The standing order exists because people got tired of finding out which kind of week it was.
No. Two ovens and one pair of hands means collection only. It is the reason the bread is what it is rather than what it could be at scale.
No, and it would not be safe to claim otherwise — everything is made in a room full of wheat flour.

items.q: What if I cannot make Saturday morning?
items.a: Tell us by Friday and it moves to the following week at no charge. Uncollected bread after nine goes to the queue rather than the bin.

sections.heading: Orders close Thursday at 8pm
sections.intro: 140 loaves, then the list closes. The standing order is the only way to be certain.

legal.deliverable: the bread and standing orders described on this site
collects: Your name, email address and order, entered at checkout so we know whose loaf is whose.
Nothing is collected by reading this page: no analytics, no advertising, no cookies.
legal.refund: If something is wrong with what you collected, tell us that Saturday and it is replaced or refunded. Uncollected orders are not refunded, because the loaf was baked.

footer.note: Sample build. Maplewood Bread Co. is a fictional bakery invented to demonstrate the template — the prices, the hours and the order link are not real.
